app.description: A channel-based messaging platform for team collaboration and developer integration.

notes: Tested: a custom auth config created without `oauth_redirect_uri` sends `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`. Register exactly the URI your auth config sends, or set `oauth_redirect_uri` to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` and register that instead.
Composio supports two distinct toolkits: **Slack** (user-level auth for workspace-level actions) and **Slackbot** (bot-level auth for in-channel messaging and app mentions).
Composio redirects auth requests through `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` by default, which can be customized via `oauth_redirect_uri`.
If your workspace restricts non-Marketplace apps, remember to adjust **App Management Settings** in Slack so custom credentials can connect without admin blocks.

assumption: An agent that reads and sends messages, manages channels, and searches workspace conversations on behalf of users in any Slack workspace.

verdict.headline: Slack OAuth apps can be created and distributed publicly without official Slack Marketplace review using unlisted distribution.
verdict.summary: Developers can register an app on the Slack API portal and enable public distribution immediately without submitting for Slack review. Apps can be installed across any workspace via OAuth 2.0, though target workspace admins may require internal approval if workspace security settings restrict non-Marketplace apps.

factors.detail: Apps are created immediately in the Slack API developer portal at api.slack.com/apps.
Slack review is optional and only required if listing in the public Slack Marketplace. Unlisted public apps can be installed on external workspaces without review.
No formal business registration or domain verification is required to obtain credentials or distribute unlisted apps.
No mandatory third-party security assessment or audit is required for unlisted public apps.
Slack API access and developer registration are free.
Open self-serve registration for all developers.
Unlisted apps have no user or workspace install caps. Marketplace listing requires installation on at least 10 active workspaces prior to review.
Target workspace admins may require internal app approval if App Management Settings restrict non-Marketplace apps.

phases.title: Register Slack App
phases.outcome: An unconfigured Slack app created in your developer portal with client credentials assigned.

steps.title: Create a new Slack app
steps.details: Go to the **Slack API Portal** at https://api.slack.com/apps, click **Create New App**, choose **From scratch**, enter your App Name and select your development workspace.

phases.title: Configure OAuth & Scopes
phases.outcome: OAuth redirect URLs configured and user/bot scopes assigned for the integration.

steps.title: Configure redirect URL
steps.details: Navigate to **OAuth & Permissions** in your app settings. Under **Redirect URLs**, add `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` (or your custom callback URL) and click **Save URLs**.
steps.agentAssist: Agent can verify the callback endpoint structure against Composio requirements.

steps.title: Add required User and Bot scopes
steps.details: In **OAuth & Permissions**, scroll to **Scopes**. Add necessary User Scopes (`user_scope`) such as `channels:history`, `channels:read`, `chat:write`, `files:read`, `users:read`, and `search:read` for full agent capability.
steps.agentAssist: Agent can output the exact list of required scope strings to copy-paste.

phases.title: Enable Public Distribution
phases.outcome: App configured for public distribution so it can be installed across any Slack workspace without Marketplace review.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.details: Go to **Manage Distribution** in your app settings, complete any requested basic information (app description, icon), and click **Activate Public Distribution**.

phases.title: Go live in Composio
phases.outcome: Slack integrated into Composio with your custom OAuth app credentials.

steps.title: Create custom OAuth config in Composio
steps.details: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret from **Basic Information** in the Slack app console. In Composio dashboard or via API, create a custom OAuth configuration for the `slack` toolkit using your credentials.
steps.agentAssist: Agent can run API calls to register the custom auth config with your Composio API key.

steps.title: Initiate connection in Composio
steps.details: Start a connection flow using your Composio integration to authorize your Slack workspace via the OAuth redirect.

requirements.detail: A standard Slack account and access to a development workspace to create and test apps.
Creating an app at api.slack.com/apps and configuring redirect URIs.
Enabling 'Manage Distribution' and completing required settings checks in the Slack app console.
If a target workspace restricts non-Marketplace apps, a workspace admin must grant approval during connection.

blockers.title: Workspace blocks unlisted apps
blockers.symptom: Users see 'This app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace...' or are blocked from installing.
blockers.howToProceed: Workspace admin must disable 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' in **Settings → Apps & Workflows → App Management Settings**.

blockers.title: Admin approval required during auth
blockers.symptom: Users are asked to submit a request for app approval during the OAuth flow.
blockers.howToProceed: Admin must approve the pending app request in Slack App Management, or disable 'Require approved apps' in workspace security settings.

nuances.title: Token Lifetimes & Rotation
nuances.detail: Slack user access tokens do not expire automatically unless revoked by the user or workspace admin, but token rotation features can be configured if required.

nuances.title: Rate Limits
nuances.detail: Slack API requests are rate-limited per method per workspace per app across multiple tiers, ranging from Tier 1 (1+ req/min) to Tier 4 (100+ req/min).

nuances.title: Scopes separation
nuances.detail: Slack divides permissions into Bot Scopes and User Scopes (`user_scope`). Actions requiring acting on behalf of the user must be requested under user scopes.

steps: Retrieve Client ID and Client Secret from your Slack app console (**Basic Information**).
Navigate to the Composio dashboard or use the Composio API to set up custom OAuth credentials for the `slack` toolkit.
Input your Client ID, Client Secret, and ensure the redirect URI matches `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`.
Trigger the connection session through Composio to link your Slack workspace.
